summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary Box
summaryBox.takeaway: Nomenclature codes regulate scientific naming. Binomial = Genus + Specific Epithet. Botany priority date: May 1, 1753; Zoology: Jan 1, 1758. Tautonyms are valid in zoology (ICZN) but forbidden in botany (ICNafp).

conceptBreakdown.content:
7.1 Codes of Biological Nomenclature:

Biological names are regulated by specific international codes:
• ICNafp: International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (formerly ICBN).
• ICZN: International Code of Zoological Nomenclature.
• ICNP: International Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes (formerly ICNB).
• ICTV: International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses.
• ICNCP: International Code of Nomenclature for Cultivated Plants.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.2 Universal Rules of Binomial Nomenclature (Linnaean System)
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.2 Universal Rules of Binomial Nomenclature (Linnaean System)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
TAUTONYM VALIDITY
                                │
         ┌──────────────────────┴──────────────────────┐
         ▼                                             ▼
  ZOOLOGY (ICZN)                                BOTANY (ICNafp)
  VALID / PERMITTED                           STRICTLY FORBIDDEN
  Example: Panthera panthera                  Example: Rosa rosa (Invalid)
           Naja naja                                   Malus malus (Invalid)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• Binomial Structure: Every scientific name consists of two Latinized words: Generic Name (Genus) + Specific Epithet (Species epithet).

• Language: Names are derived from Latin or are Latinized, regardless of their origin, and treated according to Latin grammar.

• Typography: In print, scientific names are italicized (e.g., *Homo sapiens*). When handwritten, the genus name and specific epithet are underlined separately (e.g., <u>Homo</u> <u>sapiens</u>).

• Capitalization: The Generic name must begin with an uppercase letter. The specific epithet must begin with a lowercase letter (e.g., *Mangifera indica*, NOT *Mangifera Indica*).

• Principle of Priority: The valid name for a taxon is the oldest name published after official starting dates:
  - Botany: May 1, 1753 (Publication of Linnaeus' *Species Plantarum*).
  - Zoology: January 1, 1758 (Publication of Linnaeus' *Systema Naturae*, 10th Edition).

• Citation of Authority: The name of the author who first validly published the name is appended in roman font (unitalicized) after the specific epithet: *Mangifera indica* Linn. or *Homo sapiens* Linnaeus, 1758.

• Tautonyms: A binomial name in which the generic name and specific epithet are identical in spelling (e.g., *Gorilla gorilla*, *Naja naja*, *Malus malus*). ICZN Rule: Tautonyms are PERMITTED in zoology. ICNafp Rule: Tautonyms are STRICTLY FORBIDDEN in botany.

• Trinomial Nomenclature: Used to designate subspecies in zoology (*Homo sapiens sapiens*, *Panthera leo persica*) or varieties in botany (*Brassica oleracea* var. *botrytis*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.3 The Nomenclature Type Specimen System (Nomenclatural Types)
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.3 The Nomenclature Type Specimen System (Nomenclatural Types)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
NOMENCLATURAL TYPE SPECIMENS
                                   │
         ┌─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┐
         ▼                         ▼                         ▼
     HOLOTYPE                   ISOTYPE                   PARATYPE
 (Primary specimen)        (Exact duplicate)         (Additional cited)
         │
         ├─────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┐
         ▼                         ▼                         ▼
     LECTOTYPE                 NEOTYPE                   SYNTYPE
 (Selected from original)   (New type replacement)   (Multiple co-types)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Taxonomic descriptions must be linked to concrete physical specimens archived in recognized herbaria or museums.

• Holotype: The single physical specimen designated by the original author at the time of publishing the species description as the official nomenclatural type.

• Isotype: An exact duplicate of the holotype collected from the same individual/population, at the same time, by the same collector (common in botanical collections).

• Paratype: Any specimen cited in the original protologue/description other than the holotype or isotype.

• Syntype: Any one of two or more specimens cited by an author when no single holotype was designated in the original publication.

• Lectotype: A specimen chosen from the original collection material to serve as the single nomenclatural type when no holotype was originally designated, or if the original holotype was lost or destroyed.

• Neotype: A replacement specimen chosen to serve as the nomenclatural type when all original material (holotype, isotypes, syntypes) has been lost or destroyed.

• Topotype: A specimen collected from the exact original geographic locality where the original type specimen was obtained.

quickRevision: Binomial = Genus (capitalized) + Species (lowercase); italicized in print, underlined separately when handwritten.
Priority starting dates: Botany May 1, 1753; Zoology Jan 1, 1758.
Tautonyms (e.g., Naja naja) = Valid in Zoology (ICZN), FORBIDDEN in Botany (ICNafp).
Types: Holotype (primary), Isotype (duplicate), Lectotype (selected from original), Neotype (replacement).
